description: How to reproduce PROC UNIVARIATE default output (Moments, Basic Measures, Tests for Location, Quantiles, Extreme Observations) with SAS-faithful formulas.

univariate_moments.title: PROC UNIVARIATE Moments use bias-corrected skewness/kurtosis and the sample (n-1) variance.
rule: Variance and Std Deviation use the sample estimator (ddof=1); Std Error Mean = Std / sqrt(n).
Skewness = (n / ((n-1)(n-2))) * sum(z^3), where z = (x - mean)/std; requires n >= 3.
Kurtosis = (n(n+1) / ((n-1)(n-2)(n-3))) * sum(z^4) - 3(n-1)^2 / ((n-2)(n-3)); requires n >= 4. This is the EXCESS kurtosis SAS reports.
Uncorrected SS = sum(x^2); Corrected SS = sum((x-mean)^2); Coeff Variation = 100 * std / mean.
numpy/pandas/scipy defaults differ (population variance, or Fisher-g skewness); implement the SAS formulas explicitly for parity.
pitfalls: scipy.stats.skew/kurtosis default to the biased (population) 'g' statistics, not SAS's bias-corrected 'G' statistics.
Using ddof=0 anywhere in the moment chain silently shifts std, CV, std-error, skewness and kurtosis.

reference_impl.note: Full Moments, Basic Measures, Tests for Location, Quantiles (PCTLDEF=5) and Extreme Observations tables as DataFrames.

univariate_location_tests.title: Tests for Location report Student's t, Sign, and Signed Rank against Mu0 (default 0).
rule: Student's t: t = (mean - Mu0) / (std/sqrt(n)); two-sided p from the t distribution with n-1 df.
Sign test statistic M = (n_pos - n_neg)/2 over the non-zero deviations d = x - Mu0; two-sided p from the binomial(n_nonzero, 0.5) tail.
Signed Rank S is centered as W+ - n_nonzero(n_nonzero+1)/4 on the ranks of |d| (zeros dropped); SAS uses a t/normal approximation for the p-value.
Drop deviations exactly equal to zero before the Sign and Signed Rank tests (SAS excludes ties at Mu0).
pitfalls: Forgetting to drop d==0 rows inflates n for the sign/signed-rank tests.
Reporting a one-sided p-value; SAS defaults to two-sided.

reference_impl.note: location_tests DataFrame (Student's t / Sign / Signed Rank) with two-sided p-values.
